poster_title: Test-Time Preference Optimization: On-the-Fly Alignment via Iterative Textual Feedback
authors: Yafu Li, Xuyang Hu, Xiaoye Qu, Linjie Li, Yu Cheng
paper_info: 2024, A framework for aligning large language models with human preferences during inference without retraining

panels.headline: Addressing unexpected or unsafe responses in LLMs without retraining
content: LLMs show impressive capabilities but may produce unexpected or unsafe responses.
Traditional alignment methods are time-consuming and hinder swift adaptation.
TPO aims to align LLMs with human preferences during inference without retraining.
Textual feedback is used instead of purely numerical rewards for preference optimization.

panels.headline: TPO performs gradient descent in textual form
content: TPO leverages the ability of LLMs to interpret and act upon reward signals during inference.
The policy model translates numerical reward signals into textual critiques and suggestions.
TPO updates responses based on textual feedback without altering model parameters.
panels.figure_caption: Framework of test-time preference optimization (TPO), shown here on a real example from AlpacaEval 2.

panels.headline: Experiments on a wide range of benchmarks
content: Experiments conducted on instruction following, preference alignment, safety, and mathematics.
panels.figure_caption: Test-time training curve for the (unaligned) SFT model and (aligned) instruct models.

panels.headline: TPO outperforms aligned models on nearly all benchmarks
content: TPO progressively improves alignment with human preferences.
The unaligned Llama-3.1-70B-SFT model outperformed its aligned counterpart after several TPO steps.
TPO scales efficiently with both search width and depth.
panels.figure_caption: Benchmark performance of the unaligned model (Llama-3.1-70B-SFT) with TPO, compared against training-time aligned baselines.

panels.headline: Introduction of TPO as a lightweight and practical alternative
content: TPO is a lightweight and practical alternative to training-time methods.
Demonstrated that TPO can achieve better alignment with human preferences without retraining.
Empirically validated TPO's effectiveness across various benchmarks and model sizes.

panels.headline: TPO offers a flexible and efficient alternative to training-time methods
content: TPO establishes a new paradigm for aligning LLMs with human preferences during inference.
Continuous refinement of model outputs based on textual feedback opens new possibilities for real-time alignment.
